name: serverless
context: Event-driven workloads where application code runs without server management, scaling automatically from zero based on event triggers while paying only for actual execution time
benefits: Cost efficiency: pay only for execution time, no idle resources
Auto-scaling: zero to massive scale automatically based on demand
No server management: managed infrastructure, no provisioning or patching
Rapid development: focus on business logic, faster time-to-market
Elasticity: handle traffic spikes without pre-provisioning capacity
Operational simplicity: no server-level operational overhead
tradeoffs: Cold starts: initial latency for idle functions (100-500ms typical)
Execution limits: timeout, memory, and disk constraints (Lambda: 15min max, 10GB memory)
Vendor lock-in: cloud-specific implementations and APIs
Testing complexity: hard to replicate environment locally
Debugging challenges: limited observability into execution
Statelessness constraint: must externalize state to managed services
use_cases: Image resizing or document conversion triggered by S3 uploads
Webhook handlers for third-party API integrations
Scheduled report generation and email dispatch
IoT device data ingestion and processing
Background job processing from message queues
API backends with sporadic traffic patterns
Real-time file validation and virus scanning
ETL pipelines triggered by file or database events
avoid_when: Applications require predictable sub-100ms latency under consistent load
Long-running computational workflows (ML training, video rendering)
Strong ACID transaction requirements spanning multiple function invocations
Deep recursion or algorithms requiring extended execution time
Applications with persistent in-memory state requirements
Complex distributed transactions requiring saga coordination
Strict compliance requirements for data locality and auditability
component_types: Function-as-a-Service (FaaS): Single-purpose stateless functions that execute in response to events
API Gateway: HTTP routing, request/response transformation, rate limiting, and authentication
Event Sources: Queue polling, stream processing, scheduled triggers, and event publishers
Backend-as-a-Service (BaaS): Managed databases, authentication, storage, and messaging services
Workflow Orchestration: Multi-step business processes using state machines (Step Functions, Durable Functions)
Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ): Failed event handling, retry logic, and error capture for async invocations
technology_stack: Compute: AWS Lambda, Azure Functions, Google Cloud Functions
API Gateway: AWS API Gateway, Azure API Management, Google Cloud Endpoints
Databases: DynamoDB, Aurora Serverless, Cosmos DB, Firestore
Storage: S3, Azure Blob Storage, Google Cloud Storage
Message Queues: SQS, Azure Service Bus, Google Cloud Pub/Sub
Workflow: AWS Step Functions, Azure Logic Apps
Monitoring: CloudWatch, Azure Monitor, Google Cloud Monitoring
Authentication: Cognito, Azure AD B2C, Firebase Authentication
anti_patterns: Monolithic Lambda: stuffing entire application logic into single large function
Synchronous Chain: creating long chains of function-to-function calls instead of async events
Ignoring Idempotency: not designing functions to safely handle retries
Synchronous Database Writes: blocking database operations within function execution
Excessive Dependencies: large deployment packages causing slow cold starts
No DLQ Strategy: failing to handle failed async invocations
VPC Penalty: placing Lambda in VPC without proper optimization causing cold start issues
Hardcoded Configuration: embedding environment-specific values instead of using parameter stores
design_principles: Single Responsibility: Each function performs one well-defined task triggered by a specific event type
Statelessness: Functions should not rely on internal state; externalize state to managed services (DynamoDB, S3, etc.)
Idempotency: Functions must produce the same result for the same input, enabling safe retries
Short Execution: Design functions to complete quickly (under 15 minutes for Lambda); use async for long-running tasks
Event-Driven: Use events (SQS, SNS, EventBridge) to trigger processing rather than synchronous chains
Graceful Degradation: Implement circuit breakers and DLQ handling for failures
Minimal Dependencies: Keep deployment packages small to reduce cold start latency
Connection Pooling: Reuse database connections across invocations to avoid exhausting connection limits
best_practices: Cold Start Mitigation: Use provisioned concurrency for latency-sensitive functions; optimize package size
Error Handling: Implement retry mechanisms with exponential backoff; use dead-letter queues for failed events
Idempotent Design: Include idempotency keys in event processing; check for duplicate processing
Resource Configuration: Right-size memory allocation; higher memory also provides more CPU
Structured Logging: Use structured logging (JSON) for better log querying and analysis
Distributed Tracing: Implement X-Ray, Application Insights, or Cloud Trace for cross-function debugging
Secrets Management: Store secrets in parameter stores (SSM, Secrets Manager) rather than environment variables
VPC Optimization: Place functions in VPC only when necessary; use NAT Gateway or VPC endpoints for private resources
Cost Monitoring: Set budget alerts; monitor invocation counts and duration; use reserved concurrency for steady workloads
Version Control: Use semantic versioning for functions; implement canary deployments for safe updates
